b01.title: A Hummingbird's Heart Beats 1,200 Times a Minute
b01.desc: For its size, a hummingbird's heart is huge. It can beat more than 1,200 times a minute. Yours beats about 70.

b02.title: Every Night This Bird Almost Shuts Down
b02.desc: At night a hummingbird can't eat, so it goes into torpor: its body cools and its heart drops from 1,200 beats a minute to about 50.

b03.title: A Hummingbird's Tongue Is Split in Two
b03.desc: The tip of a hummingbird's tongue splits in two and opens like tiny brushes to grab nectar, about 15 licks every second.

b04.title: Why Hummingbirds Can Fly Backwards
b04.desc: The secret is the shoulder: a hummingbird twists its wing almost all the way over, so it pushes air down both ways. That lets it hover, fly backwards and even flip upside down.

b05.title: This Red Throat Has No Red in It
b05.desc: A hummingbird's red throat has no red pigment. Tiny layers in the feathers bounce light, so the color flashes on and off. Anna's hummingbird uses that shine in a 100 km/h dive.
b05.credit: Photos: Blake Ross (CC BY 4.0), Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

b06.title: This 3 Gram Bird Crosses a Sea Without Landing
b06.desc: Before migrating, a ruby-throated hummingbird almost doubles its weight, then flies about 800 km nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico. The rufous hummingbird flies more than 6,000 km from Alaska to Mexico.
b06.credit: Photos: Blake Ross (CC BY 4.0), VJAnderson (CC BY-SA 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

b07.title: This Bird Builds Its Nest With Spider Silk
b07.desc: A hummingbird nest is about the size of half a walnut, made of plant fluff and held together with spider silk that stretches as the chicks grow.
b07.credit: Photo: Mike's Birds (CC BY-SA 2.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

b08.title: The Smallest Bird in the World
b08.desc: A ruby-throated hummingbird weighs about 3 grams, like a coin. The bee hummingbird from Cuba is only about 5 cm long: the smallest bird in the world.
b08.credit: Photos: Blake Ross (CC BY 4.0), Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

b09.title: Hummingbirds Can't Walk
b09.desc: Hummingbird feet are tiny. Great for gripping a branch, but a hummingbird can't really walk or hop. Even to move a few centimeters, it flies.
